lessons.title: Practice Relational Operators
lessons.description: Python provides comparison operators: == (equal), != (not equal), <, >, <=, >=. Write is_equal(a, b) and is_greater(a, b). The test checks that is_equal(5, 5) is true; is_greater(10, 3) is true; is_equal(5, 6) is false.
learning_objectives: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn, and compare values using.

lessons.title: Practice Chained Comparisons
lessons.description: Python allows chaining comparisons like min_val <= x <= max_val. Write in_range(x, low, high). The test checks that in_range(5, 1, 10) is true; in_range(1, 1, 10) is true; in_range(0, 1, 10) is false.
learning_objectives: Marsh clerks recount crates before dawn, and chain comparisons concisely.
lessons.solution_code:
def in_range(x, low, high):
    return low <= x <= high

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Comparisons — chained comparisons (Language Reference)

lessons.title: Practice Rollercoaster Entry Check
lessons.description: Finish can_ride. Determine if a person can ride a rollercoaster: age >= 10 and height_cm >= 130. The test checks that can_ride(12, 140) is true; can_ride(8, 140) is false; can_ride(12, 120) is false.
learning_objectives: Mesa potters recount crates before dawn, and apply multiple relational comparisons.
lessons.solution_code:
def can_ride(age, height_cm):
    return age >= 10 and height_cm >= 130
